name: Sake
description: Japanese fermented rice wine with a clean, nuanced flavor enjoyed warm or chilled depending on the grade.
ingredients: a handful of fresh mitsuba, chopped
instructions: Combine the short-grain rice and water in a saucepan, blender, or pitcher, stirring well.
Add the shichimi togarashi and soy sauce, stirring gently so their flavor infuses the mixture.
Heat gently over low heat (or blend, or steep, depending on the drink) until well combined and fragrant, about 5 mins.
Strain through a fine sieve to remove any solids, if needed.
Sweeten to taste with bonito flakes, adjusting gradually until the balance feels right.
Chill in the refrigerator, or pour straight over ice, depending on whether it is served cold or hot.
tips: Make a big batch and keep it chilled in the fridge — the flavor often deepens after a few hours.
Serve in a chilled glass for the most refreshing result on a hot day.
If serving warm, gently reheat just before pouring rather than letting it come to a boil.
